# opencode-read-excerpt

An OpenCode tool that reads one explicit, bounded line range from a single text file.

## What it does

`read_excerpt` returns a precise slice of a file: a single file, a single 1-based inclusive line range, between 1 and 80 lines. It is built for agents that need to verify a targeted excerpt instead of pulling in a whole file. The tool asserts its own permission action (`read_excerpt`) and does not reuse the built-in `read` permission. There is no "read everything" fallback, no globbing, no URL or shell access, and no silent correction of invalid input. The response is a deterministic, self-describing text report with the requested range, the returned lines, EOF state and status.

## Requirements / Compatibility

- OpenCode **2.3.x** (verified on **2.3.0**).
- `@opencode/plugin` **>=2.2.5 <3** (runtime peer dependency).

This package targets the **V2 plugin API** (`Plugin.define`, `ctx.tool.transform`, `ctx.permission.assert`, ordered permission rules with last-match-wins). The V1 API (`@opencode-ai/plugin`) is **not supported**. No migration of OpenCode itself is required: the plugin is loaded by OpenCode's existing plugin loader.

Compatibility has been verified only for OpenCode 2.3.0 with `@opencode/plugin` 2.2.7. Other versions are not claimed as supported, even if they may work.

## Install

Install the package in your project:

```sh
npm install opencode-read-excerpt
```

Then register it in `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-read-excerpt"]
}
```

If you want to set the permission name used for catalog visibility, pass options:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-read-excerpt",
      "options": { "permission": "read_excerpt" }
    }
  ]
}
```

OpenCode installs the npm package and loads it as a plugin. The package has **no runtime dependencies**; its only peer dependency is `@opencode/plugin`, which OpenCode provides. The entrypoint is TypeScript (`src/index.ts`) because the OpenCode runtime loads TypeScript entrypoints from npm packages natively.

## Usage

A tool call with explicit input:

```json
{
  "path": "src/example.txt",
  "start_line": 10,
  "end_line": 12
}
```

Expected output when line 12 does not exist (the file has 11 lines):

```text
File: "/abs/path/requested.txt"
Real file: "/abs/path/resolved.txt"
Requested lines: 10-12
Returned lines: 10-11 (2 lines)
EOF: yes
Status: ok
Content:
10 | prima riga
11 | seconda riga
```

Relative paths are resolved against the session/project directory that OpenCode provides. `~` is **not** expanded: paths are treated as literal or absolute.

## Tool contract

| Rule | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Name | `read_excerpt` |
| Input | `{ path, start_line, end_line }` |
| Line indexing | 1-based, inclusive on both ends |
| Range size | 1 to 80 lines |
| Scope | Exactly one file and exactly one range |
| Not supported | Globs, URLs, shell, Git, directory listings |
| Defaults | None: no implicit "read everything" |
| Invalid input | Rejected with an error, never silently corrected |
| Call count | No limit; no cumulative budget |
| Adjacent ranges | Allowed; no automatic blocking of contiguous calls |

## Permissions

The tool asserts the action **`read_excerpt`**, plus **`external_directory`** for paths outside the project. It never asserts `read`, so a `deny` rule on `read` does not disable this tool.

Default behavior: no configuration needed. Agents inherit `{ "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }`, so `read_excerpt` is allowed. Agent defaults also set `read` to `ask` on `*.env` / `*.env.*` and `allow` on `*.env.example`.

Read denied, `read_excerpt` allowed:

```jsonc
"permissions": [
  { "action": "read", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" },
  { "action": "read_excerpt", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }
]
```

`read_excerpt` allowed, external files require confirmation:

```jsonc
"permissions": [
  { "action": "read_excerpt", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }
]
```

Permission rules are an ordered array evaluated with **last match wins**, and `*` matches across `/`. If no rule matches, the default effect is `ask`.

`options.permission` (default `read_excerpt`) only affects catalog visibility: a `deny` rule with `resource: "*"` on that action hides the tool from the catalog.

## Environment files

File names `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env` and `*.env.*` are blocked. The only allowed variants are those ending in `.example`: `.env.example`, `.env.local.example`, `foo.env.example`.

The check is applied both to the requested path and to the resolved real destination (after symlink resolution), and it happens before any content is read. No permission rule can bypass this block.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | On exceed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lines per call | 80 | `E_RANGE_LIMIT` error |
| Bytes per line (UTF-8) | 16384 | `E_LINE_TOO_LONG` error |
| Bytes in formatted response | 524288 | `E_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE` error |
| Scan chunk size | 65536 bytes | — |

Exceeding a limit produces an explicit error. Content is never silently truncated.

Scanning reads the file in chunks of 65536 bytes and must traverse the whole file to determine the total line count (EOF) and to validate encoding and binary content across the entire file. The cost is therefore O(file size) per call, while memory is O(chunk + excerpt).

There is no limit on the number of calls, no cumulative budget, and no automatic blocking of adjacent ranges.

## Output format

Each successful call returns a fixed-format text report:

```text
File: "<absolute requested path>"
Real file: "<absolute resolved path>"
Requested lines: <start>-<end>
Returned lines: <first>-<last> (<n> lines)
EOF: yes|no
Status: ok|start_beyond_eof|empty_file
Content:
<line number> | <line content>
```

- `EOF: yes` when the last requested line is at or before the end of the file; otherwise `no`.
- `Status: ok` for a normal excerpt.
- `Status: start_beyond_eof` with `Returned lines: none (0 lines)` when the start line is beyond EOF.
- `Status: empty_file` for an empty file.

Line content excludes the `CR` of a `CRLF` terminator; an isolated `CR` is preserved as content. A leading UTF-8 BOM is removed.

## Errors

Failures are reported as `read_excerpt: <CODE>: <message>`.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `E_INPUT` | Missing or malformed tool input |
| `E_PATH` | `path` is missing or not a valid string |
| `E_PATH_SYNTAX` | Path syntax is invalid |
| `E_START_LINE` | `start_line` is not a positive integer |
| `E_END_LINE` | `end_line` is not a positive integer |
| `E_RANGE_ORDER` | `end_line` is before `start_line` |
| `E_RANGE_LIMIT` | Range exceeds 80 lines |
| `E_ENV_BLOCKED` | Requested or resolved target is a protected environment file |
| `E_CONTEXT` | No session/project context available for relative resolution |
| `E_NOT_FOUND` | File does not exist |
| `E_PATH_RESOLUTION` | Path could not be resolved |
| `E_NOT_REGULAR` | Target is not a regular file |
| `E_PERMISSION_NOT_GRANTED` | `read_excerpt` permission was not granted |
| `E_ACCESS` | Filesystem access denied |
| `E_PATH_CHANGED` | Path changed between resolution and read |
| `E_FILE_CHANGED` | File changed during the read |
| `E_ENCODING` | Content is not valid UTF-8 |
| `E_BINARY` | Content looks binary (NUL or forbidden control characters) |
| `E_LINE_TOO_LONG` | A line exceeds 16384 bytes |
| `E_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE` | Formatted response exceeds 524288 bytes |
| `E_ABORTED` | Operation was aborted |
| `E_IO` | Filesystem I/O error |

Forbidden control characters are U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, U+000E–U+001F and U+007F. UTF-8 is mandatory: UTF-16/UTF-32 BOMs are rejected.

## Local verification

From a cloned repository:

```sh
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm pack --dry-run
```

To try the plugin in an isolated OpenCode instance without touching global configuration, redirect the XDG directories and use a test config in a temporary directory:

```sh
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/opencode-test/config
export XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/opencode-test/data
export XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/opencode-test/cache
export XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/opencode-test/state
mkdir -p "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME"
```

Test `opencode.jsonc` inside that temporary config directory:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "/absolute/path/to/the/repository" }
  ]
}
```

Use absolute paths only, and do not use `~`: it is not expanded.

## Publishing

The package is **not published yet**. Remaining steps:

1. Complete the missing npm metadata: author/maintainer, repository URL, homepage, issue tracker, and copyright holder. These values are intentionally not filled in and must be provided by the maintainer.
2. Verify that the name `opencode-read-excerpt` is available on the npm registry before publishing.
3. Run `npm pack` and then `npm publish`.
4. Tell users to load it into OpenCode with `opencode plugin add opencode-read-excerpt`, or via the `plugins` entry in `opencode.jsonc`.

Git push and release steps remain manual.

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`.

## Security notes

- No telemetry.
- No network access during tool execution.
- The tool grants no global permissions and does not modify agent permissions.
- Relative paths are resolved against the OpenCode session/project directory, not the home directory.
- Excerpts that are already authorized internally do not require repeated confirmations.
